title: Core Agent Loop & Session Engine
description: The foundational agent loop, message persistence, and session lifecycle. Includes the prompt() entry point, loop() iteration, processStream() for AI SDK stream handling, session CRUD, message/part persistence, and AbortController propagation.
business_goal: Deliver the irreducible kernel of the agent — without this, nothing else works. Every other epic depends on the loop and session engine.
acceptance_criteria: prompt() creates or resumes a session and drives loop() to completion
loop() iterates: load messages → build system → resolve tools → stream → check finish → repeat
processStream() handles all AI SDK stream events (text, tool, step, reasoning, error)
Session CRUD operations (create, get, touch, setTitle, list) are functional
toModelMessages() correctly replays full conversation history for LLM context
AbortController is propagated through the entire call chain
cancel() API is exposed and halts execution cleanly

title: Profile System
description: Profile-driven agent identity — every session has exactly one active profile declared via YAML config. Profiles bind system prompt, tools, skills, and optionally a model override. Supports global → project config hierarchy and runtime switching.
business_goal: Enable noise reduction by ensuring agents only carry the tools and skills they need. Prevents context bloat and makes agent behaviour deterministic and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: YAML config hierarchy (global → project) is merged correctly
resolveProfile() resolves: explicit ID → config default → built-in coder fallback
readPromptFile() parses YAML frontmatter for name and description
project-level profile_overrides support additive skills_add and tools_add
Sub-agent profile validation warns and strips unknown profile IDs
/profile <name> switches profile at runtime without session restart
Profile cache is reset correctly on profile switch

title: Tool System
description: Universal ToolDef interface, tool registry with validation, external tool loading from filesystem, built-in tools (read, compact, skill), and permission-gated execution via toAITool().
business_goal: Allow users to extend the agent with custom tools that adapt it to any workflow, stack, or system — without modifying the harness. The tool system is the primary extensibility surface.
acceptance_criteria: ToolDef<T> interface with Zod parameter schema is enforced
Registry validates and rejects tools missing id, description, Zod parameters, or execute function
External tools load from ~/.config/quark/tools/{id}.ts with graceful error notifications on failure
Built-in tools (read, compact, skill) are registered and functional
toAITool() correctly converts ToolDef to AI SDK tool with permission and hook wiring
Only profile-declared tools are registered per session — no global tool pool leakage

title: Skill System
description: Progressive 3-level skill disclosure (L1 metadata in prompt, L2 full instructions on demand, L3 filesystem resources never loaded). Skill discovery from project and global dirs, profile binding, and buildSkillTool() as a registered tool.
business_goal: Minimise token cost while enabling on-demand specialised behaviour. Skills let the agent learn domain-specific workflows without paying the full context cost at startup.
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md files are discovered from .quark/skills/ (project) and ~/.config/quark/skills/ (global)
Project skills override global skills of the same name
profileSkills() filters to profile-bound names; L1 metadata (~100 tokens) is injected into system prompt
loadSkill() loads full SKILL.md body (L2) only when triggered via skill tool call
buildSkillTool() wraps discovery and loading as a registered tool
L3 resources (scripts, references) are never loaded into context

title: Permission System
description: Wildcard rule evaluation (allow/deny/ask) with async ask/respond lifecycle. Supports session-scope rules, CorrectedError/RejectedError feedback to model, and automatic cleanup.
business_goal: Allow the agent to operate safely and autonomously by gating tool execution through configurable rules — without requiring human confirmation for every action.
acceptance_criteria: wildcardMatch() supports *, ?, and optional trailing ' *' patterns
evaluate() applies last-matching-rule-wins across merged rulesets
ask() enqueues a PendingRequest, emits permission-request event, and returns a Promise
respond() resolves or rejects pending requests; 'always' creates session-scope rule and auto-resolves matching pending requests
CorrectedError delivers user feedback back to the model; RejectedError halts execution
DeniedError is thrown immediately on hard deny rules
clearSession() cleans up pending requests on session end
disabled() correctly identifies tools blanket-denied by deny + * rules

title: Context Compaction
description: Auto and manual context compaction with pluggable methods. Includes shouldCompact() heuristic, deduplication guard, general (new-session) and anchored (in-session) compaction strategies, plugin hook for context injection, and TUI/tool triggers.
business_goal: Enable agents to survive long sessions without losing work when the context window fills up. Compaction preserves continuity while resetting token budget.

user_stories.title: Compaction chain linking
user_stories.story: As a user, I want compaction to link the old session to the new session and store the summary so that the agent can look back at previous sessions in the compaction tree.
acceptance_criteria: When compaction creates a new session, the summary and link back to the old session are stored somewhere discoverable
The agent can traverse the compaction chain to find previous session IDs

user_stories.title: read_session tool
user_stories.story: As a user, I want the agent to have a read_session tool so it can read previous sessions in the compaction chain and recover details lost during summarization.
acceptance_criteria: read_session(<sessionId>) returns the conversation history of a previous session in the compaction chain
The tool is scoped to the current session's compaction ancestry — not arbitrary sessions
shouldCompact() triggers when estimated tokens >= threshold × context_window (default 95%)
compact-resolver.ts deduplicates concurrent compaction requests on the same session
General method creates a new session seeded with LLM summary + N retained turns
Anchored method writes a summary anchor into the same session
session.compacting plugin hook allows injection of extra context strings into summary
/compact TUI command and compact tool both flow through compact-resolver
Auto-compaction can be disabled via config (auto: false)

title: Provider & Model System
description: Multi-provider routing with GitHub Copilot as primary, native Anthropic API for Claude+thinking, and user-defined OpenAI-compatible providers. Includes model limit fetching from models.dev, Responses API routing for GPT-5+, and plugin-based runtime provider registration.
business_goal: Give users flexibility to run the agent on any supported LLM provider without changing the harness code. Copilot is the default; custom providers extend this without friction.
acceptance_criteria: createCopilotProvider() creates a cached provider with correct auth headers
createCopilotAnthropicProvider() routes Claude models with thinking to Anthropic Messages API
createOpenAICompatibleProvider() supports user-defined providers from config.yaml
shouldUseResponsesApi() correctly routes GPT-5+ (non-mini) to Responses API
getModelLimit() retrieves token limits from models.dev cache; cache refreshes every hour
provider.request.before plugin hook fires before model creation and can override provider/model
API key resolution supports literal strings and env:VAR_NAME indirection

title: Plugin System
description: Drop-in TypeScript plugins loaded from ~/.config/quark/plugins/*.ts with 10 typed hook points covering session, tool, provider, and loop lifecycle. Error-isolated loading with runtime provider registration support.
business_goal: Enable power users and platform engineers to extend or customise agent behaviour (telemetry, fallbacks, context injection) without forking the harness.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin files in ~/.config/quark/plugins/*.ts are loaded asynchronously at bootstrap

All 10 hook points are callable: provider.request.before, provider.request.error, session.created, session.idle, session.error, session.compacting, tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, loop.step.before, loop.step.after
fireHook() runs all handlers sequentially and returns final mutable output
Plugin load failures emit notifications but never crash the agent
registerProvider() in PluginContext enables runtime provider registration without config file changes
output object is mutable per hook — plugins can modify provider, model, args, and injected context

title: Sub-Agent System
description: Hierarchical session spawning via --sub-agent CLI flag, real-time event streaming from child to parent via stderr NDJSON, and TUI SubAgentView rendering nested tool activity inline.
business_goal: Enable the agent to delegate specialised tasks to child agents with separate profiles, maintaining observability of the full agent tree from the parent TUI.
acceptance_criteria: --sub-agent flag reads QUARK_SESSION_ID and creates a child session with kind: subagent
QUARK_SESSION_ID is propagated to child processes automatically
event-writer.ts writes structured NDJSON events to stderr during sub-agent runs
Parent Bash tool parses stderr NDJSON and re-emits as subagent-* events on the parent bus
TUI SubAgentView renders nested tool activity inline under the parent tool call
listChildSessions() enables session tree queries
Profile declares sub_agents: [id1, id2]; unknown IDs are warned and stripped

title: Interactive TUI
description: Full terminal UI built on OpenTUI + SolidJS with reactive rendering, slash commands, permission overlays, session/model pickers, @file mention autocomplete, image paste, diff view, token/cost display, and theme adaptation.
business_goal: Provide a rich, keyboard-driven interactive experience for power developers using Quark as a daily driver for complex coding tasks.

user_stories.title: /undo — revert LLM file changes
user_stories.story: As a user, I want an /undo slash command that reverts file changes the agent made, so I can quickly recover from unwanted modifications.
acceptance_criteria: /undo is available as a slash command alongside /help, /new, /compact, etc.
/undo reverts files the agent modified back to their pre-session state (e.g. git HEAD)
/undo shows a summary of what was reverted
TUI renders at 60fps with full-terminal scrollable message area and sticky-bottom auto-scroll
Slash commands (/help, /new, /sessions, /compact, /clear, /model, /profile, /exit) are functional
@file mention triggers fuzzy autocomplete and inlines file content as context
Image paste via Ctrl+V creates image chips with Tab navigation and Backspace removal
Permission prompt overlay responds correctly to a (allow once), o (always), r (reject) keys
Session picker and model picker overlays support arrow key navigation
Token usage, cost, and model are displayed in the footer bar
Diff view renders syntax-highlighted unified diffs for file edits
Theme adapts automatically to terminal background (dark/light detection)
Undo/redo in input (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) works correctly
Up/Down arrow history navigation in chat input (session-scoped history with draft restore) — works like a terminal shell
Notification panel uses a solid background that fills the full panel and border area for improved readability

title: Extended Thinking (Reasoning)
description: User-toggled extended thinking via Ctrl+T that routes to Anthropic Messages API for Claude models with a 10,000-token thinking budget. Reasoning parts are persisted and rendered in a collapsible TUI component.
business_goal: Give users access to deeper model reasoning for hard problems without paying the cost on every request — opt-in, not always-on.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+T toggles extended thinking on/off with a 10,000-token budget
Thinking-enabled requests are routed to the Anthopic Messages API
reasoning-start, reasoning-delta, reasoning-end stream events are handled and persisted as reasoning parts
ThinkingIndicator component renders collapsible thinking text in the TUI
Thinking budget is not applied to non-Claude models

title: Retry & Error Recovery
description: Automatic retry with exponential backoff and jitter for HTTP 429, 5xx, network timeouts, and overload errors. Plugin hook for custom fallback logic. In-flight tool parts marked as errored on mid-stream abort.
business_goal: Ensure resilient operation in the face of transient provider failures without user intervention, protecting long-running tasks from being lost.
acceptance_criteria: isRetryable() correctly classifies HTTP 429, 5xx, network errors, and overloaded errors as retryable
401/403 and non-429 4xx errors are not retried
Exponential backoff with jitter retries at ~1s, ~2s, ~4s, ~8s intervals capped at 30s
provider.request.error plugin hook can trigger retry with provider/model override
In-flight tool parts are marked as errored when a mid-stream abort occurs
AbortError is not retried

title: SDK & CLI Distribution
description: Quark as a publishable, embeddable SDK (@quark/sdk) and standalone CLI binary. Includes tsup bundle to ESM+CJS, full type exports, and CLI flags for all operational modes.
business_goal: Allow platform engineers and AI tool builders to embed Quark in their own systems, CI/CD pipelines, and automation scripts without running the TUI.
acceptance_criteria: tsup produces valid ESM and CJS bundles under the @quark/sdk package name
All public types are exported: ToolDef, Session, AgentConfig, ProfileDef, BusEvents, etc.
quark binary is available via bin.quark and executes correctly
CLI flags work correctly: --list-profiles, --help, --session, --parent-session, --sub-agent
SDK package version, publishing pipeline, and changelog process are defined (resolves OQ-5)
SDK_GUIDE.md references are updated from @atom/sdk to @quark/sdk (resolves OQ-7)

title: Session Title Generation
description: Automatic, non-blocking session title generation using a small model (gpt-4o-mini) in the background. Never fails the session if title generation errors.
business_goal: Improve session discoverability in the TUI session picker without adding latency to the critical path.
acceptance_criteria: Session title is generated asynchronously using small_model (default: gpt-4o-mini)
Title generation errors do not propagate to or fail the parent session
Generated title is persisted via setTitle() and reflected in the TUI session picker

title: Event Bus
description: Typed singleton event bus (TypedBus) with 30+ event types covering the full agent lifecycle — session, loop, tool, permission, compaction, and sub-agent events. TUI and CLI subscribe for real-time rendering and output.
business_goal: Decouple the agent core from all consumers (TUI, CLI, plugins, sub-agent parent) via a clean event-driven interface, enabling real-time observability without tight coupling.
acceptance_criteria: TypedBus exposes typed emit/on/off for all 30+ BusEvents
Max 100 listeners enforced to prevent memory leaks
TUI wireEvents() subscribes and dispatches all relevant bus events to SolidJS state
CLI subscribes to events and outputs structured data to stdout
Sub-agent events from child stderr NDJSON are correctly forwarded to the parent bus as subagent-* events

title: Web UI — Image Attachment Pipeline
description: End-to-end image attachment for the Quark web chat UI. Users can pick one or more images via a file picker, preview and remove them before sending, and submit them alongside their message. Sent images are rendered as thumbnails inside the user chat bubble and survive session reload. The backend contract (images: { mime, data }[] in POST /api/prompt) already exists — all work is front-end.
business_goal: Enable users to share visual context (screenshots, diagrams, mockups) with the agent directly from the web UI, unlocking image-aware responses without any backend changes.

user_stories.title: File & directory mention picker
user_stories.story: As a user of the Quark web UI, I want to click an @ button in the input toolbar to search and select files or directories so that I can mention them in my message without typing the full path manually.
acceptance_criteria: An @ button sits in the input toolbar at the same level as the attachment button
Clicking it opens an inline search popover above the textarea
The popover calls GET /api/files?q=<query> (or equivalent) and lists matching file and directory paths
Selecting an entry inserts @<path> at the current cursor position in the textarea and closes the popover
Typing after @ in the textarea also triggers the same popover (keyboard parity with the button)
Popover closes on Escape or click-outside without inserting anything

user_stories.title: Slash command picker button
user_stories.story: As a user of the Quark web UI, I want to click a / button in the input toolbar to browse and select available slash commands so that I can trigger agent actions without remembering exact command names.
acceptance_criteria: A / button sits in the input toolbar at the same level as the attachment button
Clicking it opens an inline command palette above the textarea listing all supported commands: /help, /new, /sessions, /compact, /clear, /model, /profile
Each entry shows the command name, a short description, and optional usage hint (sourced from the same command registry as the TUI, src/tui/commands.ts)
Selecting a command inserts /<command> into the textarea and closes the palette
Typing / in the textarea also triggers the same palette with live prefix filtering (keyboard parity with the button)
Palette closes on Escape or click-outside without inserting anything
InputArea exposes an attachment button that opens a native file picker (accept: image/*, multiple)
Selected images are encoded to base64 and held in component state with mime type and preview URL
Thumbnail previews are shown above the textarea; each has an ✕ button to remove it before send
Files over 5 MB are rejected with an inline error toast and not added to the queue
sendMessage() in app.tsx forwards images: [{ mime, data }] to POST /api/prompt
Attachment state is cleared after a successful send
Sent images are rendered as thumbnails inside the user chat bubble in message-item.tsx
ImagePart is added to the MessagePart union in state.ts so images survive session reload
Text-only messages continue to work exactly as before
@ button and / button sit in the input toolbar alongside the attachment button
Both pickers can be triggered by button click or keyboard (@ and / typed in textarea)

title: Quark Desktop V1 — Shared Diff Workspace
description: macOS-first Tauri 2 + React/TypeScript desktop app with Quark core as a sidecar binary. Three-pane layout (file tree, shared diff/source/preview workspace, agent chat) where human and agent share a middle-pane diff review before file writes happen. The first proof is the diff review loop: agent proposes edit, middle pane shows diff, user approves/rejects, only approval triggers the write.
business_goal: Give users a rich desktop experience where they can see, review, and approve every file change the agent proposes before it touches disk — building trust and enabling real collaboration in a shared workspace.

user_stories.title: Tauri shell + Quark sidecar startup
user_stories.story: As a macOS user, I want to open the Quark Desktop app and have it automatically start the Quark backend server so that the chat and workspace are ready without manual setup.
acceptance_criteria: Tauri app compiles and opens a native macOS window
Quark core is compiled with Bun --compile and configured as a Tauri externalBin sidecar
On app launch, Tauri spawns the sidecar, waits for GET /api/health (200), then passes the backend URL to the React frontend
Sidecar shutdown is clean on app quit
The sidecar uses the same REST/WebSocket API as the existing web server

user_stories.title: Three-pane layout shell
user_stories.story: As a desktop user, I want a three-pane layout with a resizable file tree, a middle workspace, and a chat panel so that I can navigate files, review content, and talk to the agent in one window.
acceptance_criteria: Left pane renders a file tree (project directory listing)
Middle pane supports mode switching between diff review, source editor, and HTML preview
Right pane renders the existing Quark chat UI (React SPA components from src/web/client)
Pane widths are resizable via drag handles
Layout is responsive and fills the Tauri window

user_stories.title: Diff review — agent edit preview before permission
user_stories.story: As a desktop user, I want to see exactly what the agent will change in a file before it writes, and choose to approve, always-approve, reject, or correct the change — all from the middle pane.
acceptance_criteria: When the agent emits a tool-input event for edit or write with diff metadata, the middle pane switches to diff review mode
The diff review shows a unified diff with context lines, removals (-), and additions (+)
User can click Approve (once) → POST /api/permission { reply: 'once' } → tool executes
User can click Always Approve → POST /api/permission { reply: 'always' } → session rule created + tool executes
User can click Reject → POST /api/permission { reply: 'reject' } → tool blocked
User can edit the proposed code inline and click Correct → POST /api/permission { reply: 'correct', correction: '...' } → model receives feedback
After approval and tool execution (tool-end event), the file is reloaded in the source editor and HTML preview (if applicable)
Rejected tools do not write to disk

user_stories.title: Source editor with file tree navigation
user_stories.story: As a desktop user, I want to click a file in the left pane and see its content in a syntax-highlighted CodeMirror editor in the middle pane so that I can read and edit files alongside the agent conversation.
acceptance_criteria: Left pane file tree lists files in the project workspace directory
Clicking a file loads its content into the middle pane CodeMirror editor via GET /api/workspace/file
Unsaved human edits are held in desktop draft state (not written to disk)
A Save button writes draft content to disk via POST /api/workspace/file
Syntax highlighting works for TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, Markdown, HTML, and CSS

user_stories.title: HTML preview pane
user_stories.story: As a desktop user, I want to see a live preview of the HTML file I'm working on in the middle pane so that I can verify visual changes the agent makes without switching to a browser.
acceptance_criteria: When an HTML file is selected in the file tree, the middle pane can switch to Preview mode
Preview mode renders the HTML file content in a sandboxed iframe
After an agent edit is approved and written to disk, the preview reloads automatically
Preview handles basic HTML + inline CSS + inline JS

user_stories.title: Workspace file API endpoints
user_stories.story: As a desktop client, I need REST endpoints to read and write files in the workspace so that the file tree, source editor, and human saves work without direct filesystem access from the frontend.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/workspace/file?path=... returns { content, mtime, size } for a valid file path
GET returns 404 for non-existent files and 403 for paths outside the workspace
POST /api/workspace/file with { path, content } writes content to disk and returns { ok: true }
POST validates the path is within the workspace directory
Both endpoints are served by the same Bun HTTP server as the existing REST API

user_stories.title: Chat context passing — agent aware of desktop state
user_stories.story: As a desktop user, I want the agent to know which file I'm looking at and any unsaved edits I've made so that it can give more relevant responses without me explaining the context manually.
acceptance_criteria: When sending a chat prompt, the desktop includes an optional context field in POST /api/prompt
The context field contains: active file path, active view mode, and unsaved draft content (if any)
Backend prepends the context as a system-level message part before the user's text
Messages sent without context work exactly as before

user_stories.title: Existing web UI preserved
user_stories.story: As a developer, I want the existing Quark web UI (src/web/) to continue working without regressions so that browser-based users are not affected by the desktop app work.
acceptance_criteria: `bun run src/web/server.ts` starts and serves the web UI exactly as before
All existing web UI tests pass unchanged
The desktop React app imports shared chat components from src/web/client without modifying their internals
REST API extensions (workspace file endpoints, context field) are additive — existing endpoints unchanged
Tauri app opens a native macOS window and starts the Quark sidecar automatically
Three-pane layout renders: file tree (left), diff/source/preview (middle), agent chat (right)
Agent edit/write tool calls show a diff in the middle pane before permission is granted
User can approve (once or always), reject, or correct the proposed diff from the middle pane
Only approved tool calls write to disk; rejected calls are blocked
Source editor (CodeMirror) loads files from the workspace with syntax highlighting
HTML preview renders selected HTML files in a sandboxed iframe and reloads after agent writes
Unsaved human edits are held in draft state; explicit save writes to disk
Chat context includes active file and draft state so the agent sees what the user sees
Existing web UI (src/web/) and TUI work without regressions
GET /api/workspace/file and POST /api/workspace/file work correctly with path validation
POST /api/prompt accepts optional context field and prepends it to the user message

title: /goal Command — Autonomous Goal-Driven Agent Loop
description: A /goal slash command that receives a user goal, generates a plan of atomic verifiable tasks, executes them one-by-one with fresh context per task, verifies deterministically, tracks progress in an append-only file, and enters explore mode with delta tasks if the plan is exhausted but the goal isn't met. Built on the Ralph Wiggum pattern — fresh context each iteration, progress on disk, no context compaction needed.
business_goal: Enable Quark to autonomously complete complex multi-step goals without human hand-holding between steps.
acceptance_criteria: /goal command generates a plan with atomic verifiable tasks
Tasks execute sequentially with fresh context per task
Deterministic checks verify each task
Progress tracked in single append-only progress.md
Final judge + explore mode for gap handling
Auto-approve mode prevents permission prompts
Ctrl+C preserves state; /goal resume resumes
Debug traces in verbose mode
Existing agent loop unchanged
